name: Sarjeant Gallery
funding: Whanganui District Council ($26.1M) led the NZ$79.4M rebuild with the Ministry for Culture and Heritage, Lottery Grants Board, Provincial Growth Fund, Stout Trust and other unnamed trusts.

name: Fundación Casa de los Tres Mundos
funding: Small cultural foundation built with German, Austrian, Swiss and Dutch government grants and the City of Granada; closed by the Nicaraguan state in 2024.

name: Centro de Arte Fundación Ortiz-Gurdián
funding: Private family foundation (founded 1996, León museum opened 2000) paid for by founders Ramiro Ortiz Mayorga and Patricia Gurdián, Banpro and Grupo Promerica.

name: Musée National Boubou Hama
funding: National museum of Niger. No source names who funds it.

name: Museum of West African Art (MOWAA)
funding: Founding partners: Edo State Government, Germany's Foreign Office, Mellon Foundation, British Museum, PI Trust. Leadership Circle donors include NNPC Seplat Energy, Lekoil Nigeria and Azura Power West Africa.

name: CCA Lagos (Centre for Contemporary Art)
funding: Founded 2007 by Bisi Silva with her own money. A March 2022 Sotheby's benefit auction raised US$1M toward a permanent home in Yaba.

name: G.A.S. Foundation (Guest Artists Space)
funding: Primarily funded by the Yinka Shonibare Foundation at its 2019 launch. Donors include Terra Foundation, Deutsche Bank, Afreximbank, Still Earth Holdings, British Council and Pro Helvetia.

name: Lagos Biennial
funding: Small artist-run biennial by Àkéte Art Foundation. Funded by Terra, Ford and Rockefeller Brothers Fund.

name: National Museum, Lagos
funding: Federal Government through the National Commission for Museums and Monuments; IHS Nigeria, a telecom-tower company, funded a 2026 renovation. A Ford Foundation refit stalled.

name: Yemisi Shyllon Museum of Art
funding: University museum opened 2019, endowed by collector Prince Yemisi Shyllon; free entry from June 2026 paid by Aisha and Gbenga Oyebode.
